pitfalls: Weight storage does not set the GPU compute precision: request GpuOptions(precision = FP32). The fp16 paths change answers: S26 Hexagon NPU (JIT, fp32 graph) 685/706 same argmax with probabilities off by up to 0.418; Mac Metal at its default fp16 precision 375/400 (card 'fp16 and the NPU', 'Measured quality and performance').

The graph takes host-built inputs: inputs_embeds [1,512,384] from julia1_token_table_fp16.bin ([256000,384] little-endian float16 rows, padding positions included), attention_mask [1,512] (1 real / 0 pad), qtype_onehot [1,3] (choice / score / noul); output token_logits [1,512], read at the <mask> marker positions; softmax at temperature 1 runs on the host (card 'Host contract').

Sequence: <bos> '{type} question: {question}' <eos> <mask> ' option0' <mask> ' option1' … <eos> state <eos>; 2 to 20 options, at most 48 tokens each; a request that does not fit raises an error, nothing is truncated (35 of the 2,000 typed-decisions questions need more than 512 tokens and fit the S1024 graph) (card 'Host contract').

The graph computes LayerNorm on x*2^-k with eps*2^-2k (k = 8 in layers 12-21 and the final norm, k = 2 in the head and scorer norms), uses -1e4 attention masks and scales q by 1/8 before QK^T; exact in fp32 (bit-identical token logits), finite but not the same answers in fp16 (card 'fp16 and the NPU', 'Provenance').

The float16 token table changes no answer and moves probabilities by up to 0.0077 (desktop CPU and S26 GPU); the host lookup is outside the measured graph time (Kotlin loop 19.0 ms float32 table / 23.6 ms float16 table per question in the gate app) (card 'Files', 'Measured quality and performance').

Validated against the author's runtime (CPU FP32), not task accuracy; one phone (Galaxy S26 SM-S942Q, LiteRT 2.2.0 Kotlin CompiledModel); English text only; S26 GPU explicit FP32: 706/706 same answers with the shipped float16 table (max probability difference 0.0077, median 111.8 / 112.1 ms, second session) and 706/706 with a float32 table (0.00005, 80.7 ms, first session); desktop CPU 2,065/2,065 rows (card 'Limits', 'Measured quality and performance').
